output.name: Nalsa — The Mended Gull (The Windward Reach)
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the Gale Tavo caught the first kite that had flown too close to the cut and tore its wings. Ennu the Kite-Wright found it in the surf under the cliffs, cold and bent, and sat up three nights with cloth and whalebone. Ennu stitched the tail back with sinew, bent the wings to the shape a gull holds when it turns into the wind, and set it aloft. The Gulls watched; it flew badly, then well. It circles the north and never quite comes down. The Windward Gull carries messages on the north-east wind, close enough to the Gale that Tavo grows fond of her; the mended bird watches. Sokul, on the north ledges, says it dips a wing at boats in trouble. Hesk counts it on the Reel each winter. Its tail is the bright knot Tesk, where Ennu's last stitch went. If you are caught in a gale, look up and find the bird with the mended wing. It does not come down for prayers, but it turns, and a boat that is turned has room to live.
output.finding: Find the Windward Gull, then look a little under a hand-span to its south-west for the bird with the mended wing, which circles there and never quite comes down.
